data.name: Sourab
data.gender_notes: Sourab is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Sourab is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Surya' which means Sun. The name Sourab is believed to represent the golden light of the sun and the inner strength and bravery it embodies. The name Sourab carries the meaning “Sun, Brave, Golden” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sourab usually hope their child will grow to embody sun, brave, golden and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sourab is a divine name, derived from the Sanskrit word 'Surya'. It represents the sun, the source of all life and energy. It is a symbol of strength, courage, and vitality. It is believed that those named Sourab are blessed with inner strength and a strong will to overcome any obstacles.
data.etymology: Sourab belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sun, Brave, Golden.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sourab total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sourab holds a rich cultural significance in Hindu mythology. In Indian mythology, the sun is considered as a vital source of energy and life. Worshipping the sun has been an essential part of various Hindu rituals and practices. Having the name Sourab, which is derived from the Sanskrit word for sun, would be seen as a sign of being connected to the divine cosmic energy of the sun, instilling a sense of vitality, strength, and passion.
data.spiritual_significance: Beyond its cultural significance, the name Sourab also holds great spiritual significance. In Hinduism, the Sun is believed to represent the god Surya. Sourab, derived from Surya, is a reminder of the innate spiritual power and inner light that exists within each individual. It is believed to represent the radiant and indomitable spirit, strength, and resilience that one can tap into in times of adversity. It also suggests that the person named Sourab is a symbol of positivity and vitality, spreading light and warmth in the world around them.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sourab: Sun's radiance embodied. This name signifies the inner brilliance and brightness, inspiring courage and strength, like the unyielding Sun in the vast cosmos.

historical_references.reference: Sourab was a legendary king of ancient India, who ruled the kingdom of Haihayas in the Mahabharata era. He is most famous for his victory over the demon king Indrajit in the Battle of Chitrasalva.

historical_references.reference: Sourab was also a celebrated warrior and an important character in the epic poem 'Mahabharata'. He was the son of King Bhagiratha of the Lunar Dynasty and is revered as a great hero in Hindu mythology. He played a significant role in the Kurukshetra war.
